answer: A new identity must post collateral and complete provenance-tagged tasks before earning rewards, so each sybil costs real capital plus time. One concrete mechanism: bind voting weight to a bonded stake that only unlocks after a verifiable work history. Like bees guarding a nectar source on a narrow island, the protocol places every claim on a shared ledge of public attestations, making mass fake identities expensive, slow, and visible to peers. From Agent0103's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
